title: FILE STORAGE AND SYNC (DROPBOX)
subtitle: Syncing a 50 GB file after a one-byte edit should not mean uploading 50 GB again.
footer: DDIA: Ch 5 conflicts · Ch 11 change log / cursor   ·   Similar: Video platform · Photo sharing

items: Split files into chunks fingerprinted by hash, and upload only the chunks the server doesn't already have.
Upload and download directly to object storage with presigned URLs.
Other devices follow a per-user change log with a cursor and fetch only what changed.
Upload and download files (up to 50GB)
Automatic sync across a user's devices
Share files and folders
Resumable uploads
Changes visible on other devices within seconds
Durable (S3 11 nines)
Bandwidth-efficient sync
Large files chunked at ~5MB: a 50GB file = 10k chunks.
Only changed chunks are re-uploaded, so a 1-byte edit sends 5MB, not 50GB.

Naive: upload the whole file through the API. A 50GB upload dies at 99% and starts over.
Split into ~5MB chunks; upload directly to S3 via presigned URLs, which is resumable and parallel.

items: Split into ~5MB chunks; upload directly to S3 via presigned URLs, which is resumable and parallel.
Fingerprint each chunk, using content-defined chunking so an insert near the start doesn't shift every boundary.
Other devices follow a per-user change log with a cursor (long-poll or WebSocket), fetch the metadata diff, and download only the changed chunks.
Resume after failure?
The server knows which chunk hashes exist; the client re-sends only missing ones.
How do devices learn about changes?
Change log + cursor per device; long-poll or WebSocket notifications.
Edits on two offline devices?
Upload carries a base version; if stale, save a "conflicted copy" (DDIA Ch 5 multi-leader conflict).
Trust the client said "done"?
Verify via S3 event or ETags before marking the file version committed.
Proxying file bytes through API servers, and re-uploading whole files on small edits.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
